product_overview: Backend service to create and manage student tasks and calendar events, with attention to reliable date parsing, conversation-memory safety, and error-recovery behavior when orchestration tools are used. Exposes HTTP endpoints for programmatic task and calendar operations used by a Streamlit front end and RAG/agent tooling.
core_goals: Provide stable CRUD endpoints for tasks and calendar events that integrate with the front-end and agent tools.
Prevent conversation-memory growth and token-overflow from agent/tool interactions by enabling truncation/summarization and diagnostics.
Add safe error-recovery behavior to avoid infinite retry loops between agent and tools.
Ensure consistent Streamlit UI state and LangGraph/internal memory alignment to avoid 'ghost' conversations.
Make relative/ambiguous date parsing robust across month boundaries and edge cases (end-of-month, leap years).
Provide diagnostic operations (snapshots, truncation, recovery attempts) to support manual debugging and automated safeguards.

features.name: Task Management
features.description: Create and manage assignments (title, course, due_date). Intended for both direct user input and programmatic insertion by agent workflows; must handle absolute and relative due_date formats and surface parsing/validation errors.
user_flows: POST /task with body {"title":"Homework 1","course":"CS101","due_date":"2026-04-10"} -> Receive 200 with created_task_id "123" -> POST /calendar with body {"title":"Due: Homework 1","date_str":"2026-04-10"} -> Receive 200 with calendar_event_id "evt-456"
POST /task with body {"title":"","course":"CS101","due_date":"2026-04-10"} -> Receive 400 with validation error "title required"

POST /task with body {"title":"Essay","course":"ENG200","due_date":"next Wednesday"} -> Receive 200 with created_task_id "124" -> POST /calendar with body {"title":"Due: Essay","date_str":"next Wednesday"} -> Receive 200 but calendar stores date_str as literal/ambiguous value or stores incorrect parsed date (indicates relative-date parsing issue that requires manual verification)

features.name: Calendar Management
features.description: Create calendar events with title and date_str. Must accept ISO dates and human-relative strings but validate/normalize before persisting to avoid incorrect dates (especially across month boundaries and leap years).
user_flows: POST /calendar with body {"title":"Midterm Exam","date_str":"2026-05-15"} -> Receive 200 with event_id "evt-789"

POST /calendar with body {"title":"Project Milestone","date_str":"next month on 31st"} -> Receive 400 with parsing error "ambiguous date" -> POST /calendar with body {"title":"Project Milestone","date_str":"2026-05-31"} -> Receive 200 with event_id "evt-790"

POST /calendar with body {"title":"Group Presentation","date_str":"next Wednesday"} -> Receive 200 with event_id "evt-791" but stored_date != expected (indicates agent-relative-date conversion bug when crossing month boundary)

features.name: Memory & Error Recovery Diagnostics
features.description: Operational/debug endpoints to snapshot, summarize, truncate conversation memory and to exercise error-recovery logic. Used by operators and automated monitors to detect token overflow, state desynchronization between Streamlit and LangGraph, and infinite-retry loops between agent and tools.
user_flows: POST /debug/memory_snapshot with body {"thread_id":"streamlit_session"} -> Receive 200 with memory_summary (turn_count, token_estimate, last_messages) -> POST /debug/truncate_memory with body {"thread_id":"streamlit_session","max_turns":10} -> Receive 200 with action "truncated"

POST /debug/consistency_check with body {"thread_id":"streamlit_session"} -> Receive 200 with report {"st_session_len":5,"langgraph_turns":25} (indicates state drift) -> POST /debug/sync_request with body {"thread_id":"streamlit_session","action":"align"} -> Receive 200 with status "sync_started"

POST /debug/trigger_tool with body {"tool":"external_agent","params":{"task":"complex_rag_operation"}} -> Receive 500 tool error with trace -> POST /debug/recovery_attempt with body {"attempt":1,"max_attempts":3} -> Receive 200 with recovery_result "requeued" -> POST /debug/recovery_attempt with body {"attempt":4,"max_attempts":3} -> Receive 429 with error "retry limit exceeded" (exposes infinite-loop guard behavior)
